column1: # PikaOS-v2 package fleet: the single source of truth for what v2/pkg-build.sh
# builds (mirrors repo-tools/workflows' "one list, one build implementation").
# Format: one "<org>/<name>" per line. Blank lines and lines starting with '#'
# are ignored. The CI matrix, v2/ci/repo-index.sh and v2/build-fleet.sh all
# read this file.
# SCOPE: branding, themes, pikman, the GUI apps, and the apt/dpkg fast patches
# This list is deliberately small. It is the identity and user-facing surface of
# PikaOS-v2 -- the things that make the image look and behave like PikaOS -- and
# nothing else. The gitea offers 347 packages with a main.sh recipe; this file
# names about 20 of them.
# What was dropped, and why:
#   * Anything that takes more than a few minutes to compile. mesa, wine,
#     chromium, blender, otter-zenith and the rest are real multi-hour builds
#     that need far more than four cores; on this box they cost a day and most
#     of them fail against sid for unrelated reasons (dropped build-deps, KF5
#     packages gone from the archive). Debian already ships them, built for the
#     distribution baseline, and an image that installs them from sid gets them
#     working today. Rebuilding them for v2 buys a little speed and costs a lot
#     of reliability.
#   * Whole desktop environments (COSMIC, Hyprland, niri, river, wayfire, otter).
#     Same reasoning: thousands of packages, days of CPU, and nothing about the
#     *branding* depends on them. The ISO recipe in iso-v2/info.sh picks a
#     desktop from Debian; this list supplies the PikaOS skin on top.
#   * Hardware/device tooling, nvidia driver matrix, gaming stack. Not identity.
# The rule: if a package is not part of what PikaOS *looks* like or what the
# user *does* in the first five minutes, it comes from Debian.
# Note on the apt/dpkg fast patches
# v2/patches/apt/apt-fast.patch and v2/patches/dpkg/dpkg-fast.patch are NOT in
# this list. They are not PikaOS packages: they are performance patches over
# *upstream* apt and dpkg, so they have no git.pika-os.com repo to build from
# and cannot go through pkg-build.sh, which is built around cloning one.
# They are also currently dead files -- nothing references them. See
# v2/patches/README.md for how they are meant to be consumed and what still has
# to happen before they reach an image. That is deliberate and documented rather
# than quietly wired up: shipping a patched dpkg that silently skipped
# verification would be a far worse outcome than not shipping it.
# 1. Branding and themes
# These are what makes the image read as PikaOS rather than as Debian with a
# wallpaper. All are data-only or icon-theme rebuilds: seconds to a couple of
# minutes each, no ISA concerns (papirus is icons + XML, no compiled code).
general-packages/pika-wallpapers
general-packages/sound-theme-pika
general-packages/desktop-base
general-packages/pika-apx-configs
general-packages/pika-sources
boot-packages/plymouth-theme-pika
kde-packages/papirus-colors
kde-packages/pika-kde-settings
kde-packages/pika-kde-desktop
# general-packages/pika-lightdm: a display-manager theme, but the image ships
# GDM/SDDM, not LightDM. Excluded with the reason rather than silently.
# general-packages/pika-lightdm
# boot-packages/pika-refind-theme: this image boots GRUB, not rEFInd
# (see README); the theme would have nothing to render.
# boot-packages/pika-refind-theme
# kde-packages/supergfxctl-plasmoid: a Plasma applet, and it is already in
# iso-v2/info.sh via the Debian name plasma-supergfxctl. Rebuilding the PikaOS
# copy adds a second source for one QML file.
# kde-packages/supergfxctl-plasmoid
# 2. pikman
# The PikaOS package manager, and the one piece of userland here that is
# genuinely compiled. It is Go, so the v2 knob is GOAMD64=v2 rather than
# -march, which amd64-v2.sh already sets (see the table in README).
# Its Debian dependencies were already trimmed to what we ship (apt-utils,
# flatpak, podman), dropping the PikaOS-only pika-apx-configs and
# vanilla-apx-gui, so it installs on a plain sid base.
general-packages/pikman
custom-gui-packages/pikman-update-manager
# 3. PikaOS GUI apps
# Eight GTK4/libadwaita apps in Rust, written by PikaOS for its own image.
# These are the ones a user actually launches, and every one of them is named
# in iso-v2/info.sh's PIKA_PKGS, so they are load-bearing for the live image.
# Each is a real cargo build (a few minutes) and each pulls a Rust toolchain
# via rustup in main.sh, so they are the slowest entries in this list and the
# ones most likely to hit a crates.io API change. That is the accepted cost:
# these have no Debian equivalent, so if they do not build here the image is
# missing them.
custom-gui-packages/pika-welcome
custom-gui-packages/pika-first-setup
custom-gui-packages/pika-installer-gtk4
custom-gui-packages/pika-drivers
custom-gui-packages/pika-device-manager
custom-gui-packages/pika-kernel-manager
custom-gui-packages/falcond-gui
# 4. Identity: os-release and fastfetch
# The two things that answer "what am I running on?" -- `cat /etc/os-release`
# and the login banner. Both are branding, which is why they are here rather
# than pulled from Debian.
# general-packages/base-files
# ENABLED. Read this before assuming it is inert: it is the PikaOS os-release
# package, a repack of Debian's own base-files
# (same Maintainer, same Rules-Requires-Root, Essential: yes, Provides: base)
# carrying one substituted file:
#   PRETTY_NAME="PikaOS 4"   NAME="PikaOS"   ID=pika   ID_LIKE=debian
#   VERSION_CODENAME=nest   LOGO=pika-logo
# and debian/rules moves it to /usr/lib/os-release with /etc/os-release as a
# relative symlink, which is what systemd, fastfetch and `lsb_release` all read.
# Read this before enabling it. Two consequences that are not obvious:
#   * It REPLACES Debian's base-files rather than layering on top of it. Same
#     package name, Essential: yes, Provides/Replaces base -- so installing this
#     over a sid system takes ownership of /etc/issue, /etc/motd, the origin
#     files and the whole FHS skeleton, and its rules rewrite them with the
#     substitution above. That is intended, but it means this is not a
#     "drop it in, get a PRETTY_NAME" package: it is a fork of a package every
#     system depends on. Worth an explicit decision rather than a line in a
#     list.
#   * It is `VERSION="14"` in main.sh against a sid tree, and the debian/
#     dir is inherited from Debian, so it is Debian's 14-era packaging. If a
#     sid dh_* sequence has moved on, this will need the same shim treatment
#     as the rest of the fleet.
# Consequence for the ISO: it must stop shipping Debian's own base-files, and
# pipeline.yml's dependency check will see the swap. If that check fails after
# enabling this, the cause is the replacement, not a missing dependency.
general-packages/base-files
# general-packages/fastfetch
# The system-info banner. PikaOS ships it as a plain upstream build: main.sh
# clones fastfetch-cli/fastfetch and runs dpkg-buildpackage, and the repo's
# debian/ holds only a changelog, so dh_make generates the packaging at build
# time. There is no PikaOS logo or config in the repo -- the branding comes from
# the os-release above (fastfetch reads LOGO= and the pika logo from
# /usr/share/pixmaps), not from anything in this package.
# v2 relevance: fastfetch is C, so amd64-v2.sh applies normally.
general-packages/fastfetch
# 5. Supporting shell/profile packages
# Small, and referenced by the ISO recipe.
general-packages/pika-shell-profiles
general-packages/pika-mango
general-packages/apx
general-packages/popsicle
# 6. Meta packages
# Dependency declarations only -- no compiled code at all, seconds each. Kept
# because pika-baseos is the name the ISO and installer refer to, so dropping it
# would break the dependency closure check in pipeline.yml.
meta-packages/pika-baseos
meta-packages/pika-audio
meta-packages/pika-meta
# Deliberately absent
# kernels      v2/kernels/build-kernel.sh builds them separately; they are not
#              packages from the gitea's fleet contract and each is an hour+.
#              See the kernel section of README.
# upstream-patches/*
#              650 repos, but 626 are bare "Diff" trees with no packaging at
#              all. They are patch overlays, not buildable packages.
# boot-packages/linux-firmware
#              ~4G of firmware blobs and 15+ minutes of extraction for no
#              branding value; Debian's own linux-firmware is complete.
# boot-packages/booster
#              A boot-time microcode reassert daemon, not branding.
# gaming-packages/*, multimedia-packages/*
#              Not branding, and the heavy ones are day-long builds.
